classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish a face–base angle from an edge–base angle and use two different vertical sections of a square pyramid.

content.prompt: A right pyramid $VABCD$ stands on a square base $ABCD$ of side length $42\text{ cm}$. If each sloping face makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the base, find:

children.label: a
children.prompt: the height of the pyramid (correct to four significant figures)

answer.worked:
Let $O$ be the centre of the square base and $M$ the midpoint of $BC$. Since the pyramid is right, $VO$ is perpendicular to the base. The face–base angle is $\angle VMO=60^\circ$.

$$\begin{align*}OM&=\frac{42}{2}=21\text{ cm}\\\tan60^\circ&=\frac{VO}{21}\\VO&=21\tan60^\circ\\VO&=21\sqrt3\text{ cm}\\VO&\approx36.37\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: the angle a sloping edge makes with the base (correct to one decimal place)

answer.short:
$50.8^\circ$

Use the angle between a sloping edge and its projection onto the base.
answer.worked:
Using the centre $O$ of the base, the projection of $VC$ onto the base is $OC$. Let $\theta=\angle VCO$.

$$\begin{align*}OC&=\sqrt{21^2+21^2}\\OC&=21\sqrt2\text{ cm}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{21\sqrt3}{21\sqrt2}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac32}\right)\\\theta&\approx50.8^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: the length of a sloping edge (correct to four significant figures)
